records.summary: The Central Bank of Eswatini's evaluations team recommended in 2017 that Farmers Bank's application for a commercial banking licence be rejected, warning it would tarnish the integrity of the bank's licensing policy, and the application was turned down late that year. Governor Majozi Sithole said a royal command required him to attend a meeting about the venture on 14 July 2017, and in May 2018 finance minister Martin Dlamini told the bank that King Mswati III had ordered an investigation into its reluctance to license it. A conditional licence was issued in September 2018 after a royal command. When the bank revoked that licence on 5 October 2020 because the source of the seed capital was unexplained, an appeal chaired by commerce minister Manqoba Khumalo ruled in December 2020 that it should stand, and the bank reinstated it in January 2021 while objecting to procedural improprieties. A 2022 forensic report by Kroll, which the bank itself commissioned, said parties outside the bank had likely intervened and instructed it to proceed. What this record holds is the state's side of that: the head of state ordering an investigation into the bank's own supervisory decision, royal commands directing the governor, and a minister-chaired appeal overriding the bank's revocation. What the officials were accused of stays in the corruption case.
records.source_title: The central bank in a tiny African country tried to block a suspicious banking venture. Then the king's allies intervened. (ICIJ, Swazi Secrets)

notes: Cross-filed from corruption cases 202 and 225, which were already on the map with this source and with a second independent account in Financial Mail / amaBhungane and Finance Uncovered. No new research: the facts and the source were already filed, and the moves layer rendered Eswatini blank because nobody had asked whether the state's own acts in the episode belonged on it.
